title: Atlas DataFlow Admin Run Summary
description: Private/admin-only projection of an internal pipeline/run-evidence.schema.json record for Dashboard run discovery. This schema is a bounded, safe summary shape only -- it is not a public contract, not a release candidate, not a published release, and not publication authority. It must never be exposed through a public route. Raw absolute paths, secrets, arbitrary file contents, raw logs, and raw runtime payloads must never appear in an instance of this schema. Missing, malformed, incomplete, and unsafe source run evidence must produce a deterministic 'unavailable' or 'invalid' summary instead of a partially populated or guessed record.

_example_note.description: Optional annotation for example or demonstration artifacts only. Omit in production admin run summary records.

schema_version.description: Schema version for this admin/private run summary projection.

run_id.description: Stable run identifier carried verbatim from the source run evidence's run_identity.run_id. Must not expose private session details, raw execution identifiers, or secrets.

status.description: Deterministic readiness/status of this summary. 'available' means the source run evidence was found and is well-formed -- this includes a run whose promotion-result.json records promotion_outcome: promoted but whose registry activation has not (yet) completed, so it remains a pending/retryable promotion target rather than a finished one. 'unavailable' means no source run evidence could be located. 'invalid' means source run evidence was located but is malformed or incomplete. 'promoted' means the source run evidence is well-formed and its promotion has completion evidence: either the live dataset registry currently binds this release, or promotion-result.json's registry_update_record carries proven historical applied evidence (update_applied: true with a matching new_active_release_id) even if the live binding was later removed. A completed promoted run must never continue to be reflected as 'available' (pending promotion). This field is distinct from the underlying run_status (accepted/rejected/failed) carried inside validation_summary.

dataset_candidate.description: Best-effort dataset slug for this run, populated only when confidently resolved from the source run evidence's input/output references. Must be null rather than a low-confidence guess, and must never contain a raw absolute path. Required to be null when status is not 'available'.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the run started, carried verbatim from the source run evidence's run_timestamps.started_at. Required to be null when status is not 'available'.

trace_reference.description: Reduced, path-shaped reference to the run's primary output artifact, carried verbatim from the source run evidence's run_outputs.output_ref. Must never be an absolute filesystem path and must never embed raw artifact contents. Required to be null when status is not 'available'.

validation_summary.description: Reduced validation outcome for this run, derived from the source run evidence's run_status and, when present, failure_info. Required to be null when status is not 'available'.

outcome.description: Outcome of the underlying run. Must not expose raw exit codes, raw runtime signals, or raw error payloads.

reason.description: Optional short reduced reason for a rejected or failed outcome, sourced from the run evidence's failure_info.failure_reason or failure_info.rejection_reason. Must not embed raw log output or raw exception details.

promotion_summary.description: Sanitized promoted-state projection derived from this run's promotion-result.json, re-checked against the live dataset registry for a safe idempotence/reuse signal. Required and non-null when status is 'promoted'; absent otherwise. Present only for a registry-completed promotion -- see the 'status' field, 'registry_state', and 'registry_bound' below for how completion is resolved. Must never expose raw filesystem paths, raw registry dumps, or promotion-result.json's internal registry_update_record verbatim.

promotion_outcome.description: Carried verbatim from the source promotion-result.json's promotion_outcome. Always 'promoted' when this object is present.

release_id.description: Stable release identifier, carried verbatim from promotion-result.json's candidate_identity.release_id. Accepts both registry-normalized release id conventions (registry/validate.py's RELEASE_ID_PATTERN).

registry_state.description: Reconciliation of this completed historical promotion against the live dataset registry (Project Spec S0282, refined by S0283). registry_state is the semantic authority for what registry_bound=false means. 'active': the registry's Dataset Detail still binds this exact release as its active_release. 'superseded': the recorded Dataset Detail still exists but a different release is now its active_release -- this run stays historically promoted and its release is preserved, and the current binding is never replaced, but (S0283) it is eligible for safe create-new recovery: the generic Admin Promote route allocates a new numbered Dataset Detail for the historical release. 'missing': the recorded Dataset Detail is no longer in the registry, so this run is promotable again (preserves Project Spec S0048). All three remain top-level status 'promoted'.

current_active_release_id.description: The release_id currently bound as the live registry Dataset Detail's active_release when it differs from this run's release_id. Present only for registry_state 'superseded'; never a guessed or historical value, and never equal to release_id at the producer level.

dataset_slug.description: Candidate/base dataset slug, carried verbatim from promotion-result.json's candidate_identity.dataset_slug.

public_dataset_slug.description: The dataset registry's current public slug whose active_release matches release_id. Present only when the live registry confirms this exact release is still active; never a guessed or historical value.

registry_action.description: Safe idempotence indicator reusing the same vocabulary as the Promote action's own response. Present only alongside public_dataset_slug, when the live registry confirms this release is still the dataset's active_release.

registry_bound.description: True when the live dataset registry (registry/datasets.json) still has a Dataset Detail whose active_release matches release_id -- a 'registry_bound_promoted' run (registry_state 'active'). False when no current registry entry points to this release, but proven historical applied evidence still exists: registry_state is then either 'superseded' (the recorded Dataset Detail still exists but a newer release is active for it; the historical release is preserved and the current binding is untouched) or 'missing' (the recorded Dataset Detail is gone). In both false cases (Project Spec S0283) the run is promotable again -- superseded via safe create-new recovery, missing via S0048 re-promotion -- with registry_state as the semantic authority for which case applies. This object is present only for a completed promotion; registry_bound: false is never produced from a never-completed/unapplied provisional record -- that case leaves the run's top-level status as 'available' instead, with no promotion_summary at all.

can_promote.description: Whether the Dashboard's Promote action should call the promotion endpoint again for this run -- the backend-projected action authority. False for registry_state 'active' (repeating promotion would only re-apply an already-active binding). True for registry_state 'superseded' (Project Spec S0283: Promote creates a new numbered Dataset Detail for the historical release without replacing the current binding) and for registry_state 'missing' (Project Spec S0048: the previously promoted Dataset Detail no longer exists). Equivalently, can_promote is the negation of registry_bound for every completed promotion.

can_remove.description: Whether the Dashboard's Remove action remains available for this promoted run. Always true: removing a run only ever deletes its run artifact/directory and never mutates the registry, releases, or Dataset Details.

reason.description: Optional short, safe user-facing message describing the current promoted state -- for example that the run has already been promoted as a Dataset Detail, or that the Dataset Detail is no longer present and the run may be promoted again. Must not embed raw filesystem paths, stack traces, or raw registry dumps.

unavailable_reason.description: Deterministic reason code required when status is 'unavailable'. Must not embed raw filesystem paths or raw error text.

invalid_reason.description: Deterministic reason code required when status is 'invalid'. Must not embed raw filesystem paths or raw error text.
